issue_context.title: Throw an error when someone pastes an SVG
issue_context.body: As per discussion in https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/1250, now that we support copying to clipboard as SVG, we should throw an error when someone tries to paste an SVG into excalidraw since that won't render nicely.
comments:
Since we're allowing to paste arbitrary text into excalidraw as text elements, and our copy-as-SVG currently copies to clipboard the SVG as plaintext (we can't use `image/svg+xml` MIME type yet because of no browser support), we can't determine whether user doesn't want to in fact paste an SVG-plaintext as a text element.

If we really want to prevent pasting the SVG text copied from excalidraw, we can prepend `<-- source:excalidraw -->` to the SVG text copied to clipboard and match against this on paste.

But I'm thinking whether we should, per @vjeux' philosophy of letting users do whatever they want. Thoughts?

> Since we're allowing to paste arbitrary text into excalidraw as text elements

I thought we decided not to do that because it would complicate this exact use case. But looks like pasting arbitrary text works right now.

I'm not opposed to going back on that decision and have the person double click to start editing text and then pasting.

> I thought we decided not to do that because it would complicate this exact use case. But looks like pasting arbitrary text works right now.

IIRC I was implementing some special heuristics exactly to allow for pasting text as text elements. We don't need to get rid of it to accommodate for this issue --- if the OP behavior is desired, let's use the comment hack I proposed, which is perfectly fine. Later when `image/svg+xml` support is added, this point will be moot and we can get rid of the hack.

My concern was UX-wise, not implem-wise.
I like tagging the source anyway. So happy with that flag (even for the export).

review_comments: also fixed an unrelated bug where pasting in-app clip threw if empty
